Mesentery with its vessels divided at the level of the appendiceal base using a diathermy hook. [p505]
Base of appendix ligated with a laparoscopic pre-tied loop suture. [p506]

Appendix grasped distal to the tightened loop and cut between with scissors to avoid intra-abdominal spilling. [EDIT: endoscopic cutting stapler including healthy cecal tip if the base is necrotic] [p506]
Appendix removed via trocar or laparoscopic bag, avoiding contact with port incisions. [p506]
Visible pus removed by irrigation and suction; field checked for hemostasis. [p506]
Abdomen desufflated; trocars removed. [p506]

Grasp and open the peritoneum; suction free fluid and enlarge the opening. [EDIT: default — open medially with scalpel/cautery; send fluid for culture]
Deliver the cecum into the wound by grasping the anterior tenia coli. [EDIT: divide lateral peritoneal attachments under vision if cecum will not deliver]
Grasp the mesoappendix with Babcock forceps and divide it to the fold of Treves. [EDIT: default — cautery, or between hemostats and ligatures; keep appendix off the wound]
Crush the appendiceal base 5 mm above its origin, ligate the crushed area, and divide the appendix just proximal to the clamp. [EDIT: default — absorbable ligature; cauterize stump mucosa]
[EDIT: stump inversion not necessary; if performed — absorbable Z-stitch or purse-string through seromuscular cecal base]
Milk and return the cecum; suction the pelvis and right paracolic gutter. [EDIT: perforated case — obtain culture and irrigate to evacuate all visible pus]

name: Arm Lap Pullthrough
source_reference: operation_id: arm_lap_pullthrough · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch58 (PDF pp. 560–564)
procedure_steps: Preoperative antibiotics [EDIT: default cefoxitin]; cystoscopy to locate fistula; urinary catheter inserted.
Umbilical access established; pneumoperitoneum achieved.
Place 3-mm ports in LUQ, right flank and RUQ along anterior axillary lines [EDIT: RUQ below liver edge; direct-puncture instruments an alternative].
Incline table left-side-up in Trendelenburg to distract small bowel cephalad.
Reflect rectum cephalad; examine pelvic floor; identify and develop the space at the apex of pubococcygeus.
Incise peritoneum at the reflection with hook cautery.
Dissect mesorectum off the rectum circumferentially, staying on the rectal wall [EDIT: identify ureters and vas bilaterally; suspend bladder with abdominal-wall stay stitch if it obscures view].
Clip the rectum as it tapers into the fistula; transect distal to the clip.
Close the rectogenitourinary fistula [EDIT: default 2/0 PDS endoloop or absorbable laparoscopic suture].
On the perineum, map the centre of the superficial anal sphincter with a muscle stimulator; mark anterior and posterior limits.
Make an 8-mm midline sagittal incision in the sphincter centre; dissect subcutaneous tissue bluntly in the midline.
Under laparoscopic transillumination, pass a 25-G needle to define the pull-through tract.
Flex hips with knees to shoulders to straighten the pull-through path.
Insert radially dilating trocar along the finder-needle axis toward the apex of the pubococcygeus V, posterior to the urethra; dilate to a 12-mm perineal port.
Grasp the distal rectum with a laparoscopic Babcock via the perineal port; pull caudally, delivering it through the sphincter complex to the skin.
Fashion the anastomosis [EDIT: default 4/0 Vicryl interrupted].
Calibrate the neo-anus with Hegar dilators and record size [EDIT: age-appropriate size per Table 58.1].

Strictly nil per rectum ~2 weeks; monitor perineum for sepsis; liberal zinc barrier cream to neo-anus/buttocks. Review at 2 weeks for calibration; weekly dilatations [EDIT].

name: Arm Psarp Open
source_reference: operation_id: arm_psarp_open · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch 56 (Anorectal malformations), PDF pp. 528–539
procedure_steps: Foley catheter passed per urethra [EDIT: Coudé / lacrimal-probe guidance if catheter tends to enter rectum].
Electrical stimulator used to map the sphincter and keep the incision exactly in the midline.
Mid-sagittal skin incision made — length per defect [EDIT: full sacrum-to-anus for prostatic fistula / limited for vestibular / minimal for perineal].
Parasagittal fibres and muscle complex divided exactly in the midline with fine-needle cautery.
Levator muscle divided in the midline; muscle structures divided until the rectum is exposed.
Two silk sutures placed in the posterior rectal wall; rectum opened in the midline between them, extending distally to the fistula.
Traction silks placed on the open rectal edges; a guide stitch placed at the fistula site.
Fistula circumscribed — 6/0 silk sutures placed in a semicircle through the rectal mucosa immediately above the fistula.
Submucosal plane developed to separate rectum from urethra [EDIT: ~5–10 mm above fistula until areolar plane reached; dissect laterally first, then anteriorly].
Circumferential perirectal dissection performed between the whitish perirectal fascia and the rectal wall to gain tension-free length.
Rectal calibre assessed; taper posteriorly if oversized [EDIT: two-layer 5/0 & 6/0 braided absorbable, if performed].
Fistula closed longitudinally with a single layer of long-term absorbable suture.
Rectum placed in front of the levator and within the muscle complex/external sphincter, limits confirmed with the stimulator.
Levator posterior edge and posterior muscle complex reapproximated behind the rectum with long-term absorbable sutures, taking a bite of rectal wall to anchor it.
Anoplasty performed with 16 interrupted long-term absorbable sutures under slight tension [EDIT: 5/0–6/0 braided absorbable per child size].

Anorectal malformation — rectourethral fistula [EDIT: bulbar / prostatic], [EDIT: with prior diverting colostomy / newborn primary repair].
> Scope note: this template's fixed steps are rectourethral-fistula-specific (Foley per urethra, submucosal separation of rectum from urethra, longitudinal fistula closure, 7-day urethral catheter, full levator reconstruction). For a rectovestibular fistula or imperforate anus without fistula, replace the urethra-separation and 7-day urethral-catheter steps with the vagina-separation steps (Ch 56 — shorter incision; levator usually not reconstructed; imperforate-anus-without-fistula repaired as for rectourethral type).

Antibiotic ointment to anoplasty for 5 days; keep incision clean, do not wipe.
Discharge ~2 days (posterior approach without laparotomy) [EDIT: 3–5 days if abdominal approach].
Begin anal dilatations at 2 weeks, twice daily, up-sizing weekly to age-appropriate Hegar [EDIT: per Table 56.1]; colostomy closure once desired size reached.

name: Bladder Exstrophy Closure
source_reference: operation_id: bladder_exstrophy_closure · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch95 — Bladder exstrophy closure and epispadias (Cuckow & Lopez), pp921–944
procedure_steps: Stay suture placed through glans for retraction [EDIT: 4/0 monofilament, round-bodied needle].

Incision from midline above umbilicus, around bladder margins, forward on either side of urethral plate to the distal limit of the veru montanum; deepened with diathermy [EDIT: distal incisions left superficial at this stage].
Midline deepened above umbilicus to expose the umbilical vein without opening peritoneum.
Umbilical arteries followed as guide to the extraperitoneal plane and both divided; umbilicus freed upward.
Blunt dissection of the plane behind each rectus, in front of the ureters (stents in position), down to the pelvic floor at the bladderneck.
With a finger behind the abdominal wall, distal incisions completed with diathermy to free the bladder each side; intrapubic bar tissue exposed.
Intrapubic bar tissue divided lateral to the veru montanum to release the bladderneck for placement inside the pelvis.
Bladder dropped into the pelvis; urethral catheter secured to bladder wall [EDIT: 8 Fr feeding tube, opposed eyes, 6/0 monocryl].
Bladder edges trimmed; bladder closed from the apex [EDIT: interrupted 4/0 monocryl], continued to the proximal urethra.
Bilateral ureteric stents secured and brought out between sutures [EDIT: two feeding tubes, 6/0 monocryl]; lower sutures left untied until pelvic approximation.
Pubic-bone approximation sutures laid [EDIT: one or two mattress 0 or 1 PDS], tied after rectus approximation.
[EDIT — bilateral herniotomy if patent processus].

name: Branchial Excision Open
source_reference: operation_id: branchial_excision_open · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch 7 (Branchial cysts, sinuses, and fistulas) · PDF pp. 78–81
procedure_steps: Incise skin only with scalpel; carry dissection through subcutaneous tissue and platysma to the level of the cyst, lifting tissues with Adson's forceps and dividing with fine haemostat and electrocautery.
Retract skin/muscle flaps with a self-retaining or ring retractor to expose the cyst.
Divide the deep cervical fascia along the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid; retract the muscle away from the cyst and extend exposure anteromedially by retracting sternohyoid.
Lift and incise the fascia/soft tissue overlying the cyst to expose its superficial aspect.
Separate adjacent structures from the cyst by blunt and electrocautery dissection along the wall, avoiding rupture; take special care on the deep aspect near the jugular vein and carotid arteries.
Trace the pedicle (posterior to the jugular vein, between the carotid bifurcation) cephalad toward the tonsillar pillar; clamp and suture-ligate with fine non-absorbable suture, then divide.

[EDIT — SINUS variant: dissect the tract cephalad on itself to the tonsillar fossa (aided by a silver probe/heavy nylon passed down the tract and by the anaesthetist's finger in the tonsillar fossa exerting downward pressure); suture-ligate and divide at the end point.]
[EDIT — FIRST-CLEFT variant: protect the facial nerve (nerve stimulator); mobilise deep/superficial parotid lobe if a tract runs to the external auditory meatus.]

[EDIT — THIRD/FOURTH-POUCH variant: collar incision, mobilise (left) thyroid lobe, identify/protect recurrent and superior laryngeal nerves and parathyroids; excise entire tract to the piriform sinus, ± superior-pole/lobe resection.]
Obtain meticulous haemostasis and irrigate the wound with 1% povidone-iodine before closure.

name: Cholecystectomy Lap
source_reference: operation_id: cholecystectomy_lap · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch69 (Cholecystectomy) · PDF pp. 671–675 · post-op care per the chapter's shared Postoperative-care paragraph (p. 671)
procedure_steps: Insert three instrument ports under direct vision — one epigastric retraction port and two hand-instrument ports either side of the umbilical trocar (placed lower than in an adult in young children).
Tilt patient head-up ~30°.
Grasp the gallbladder fundus with a toothed ratcheted grasper via the epigastric port; grasp Hartmann's pouch and retract laterally and inferiorly to display Calot's triangle.

Open the peritoneum over Calot's triangle with monopolar hook diathermy, starting at the Hartmann's pouch end of the cystic duct; do not extend the cystic duct dissection medially toward the common bile duct.
Identify the cystic artery in Calot's triangle and develop two windows — one around the cystic duct, one around the cystic artery.
Apply two clips to the medial side of the cystic artery (distal end need not be clipped) and divide it before the cystic duct.
Apply two clips to the common-bile-duct side of the cystic duct and a single clip at the Hartmann's pouch side; divide the cystic duct and check for bile leak.
Dissect the gallbladder from its fossa with monopolar hook diathermy under constant countertraction, mobilising Hartmann's pouch first and working toward the fundus.
Inspect the fossa for bleeding and bile leak; control fossa bleeding with monopolar or bipolar coagulation.

Extract the gallbladder through the umbilical port (5-mm telescope moved to the 6-mm port); [EDIT: use endobag if gallbladder perforated; deliver Hartmann's pouch, aspirate bile and extract stones to disimpact if needed].
anaesthesia: General anaesthesia via endotracheal intubation with full muscle relaxation; nasogastric tube inserted to decompress stomach and duodenum. [EDIT]

Ensure large intestine, stomach and duodenum are empty. Time-out / WHO checklist confirmed — correct patient, side, procedure. Skin prepared and draped.
incision_approach: Open laparoscopy via 11-mm Hasson cannula at umbilicus; pneumoperitoneum established at [EDIT: insufflation pressure ≤12 mmHg]. [EDIT: Veress needle alternative]
closure: Desufflate the abdomen before removing trocars to avoid omental herniation. Close umbilical incision with the Hasson purse-string suture; close instrument-port fascia with [EDIT: a single absorbable suture] each; approximate skin with cyanoacrylate.

Identify and expose cystic duct; extend dissection to expose cystic artery. [EDIT: cystic lymph node often overlies the artery]
Ligate and divide the cystic artery. [EDIT: suture/ligature]

[EDIT: intra-operative cholangiogram if indicated — side hole in cystic duct near Hartmann's pouch, cannulate, prime catheter with saline, inject diluted contrast, confirm free flow into duodenum, remove catheter]
Ligate and divide the cystic duct. [EDIT: suture/ligature]
Grasp fundus; remove gallbladder from its fossa with constant countertraction to develop the plane. [EDIT: monopolar diathermy preferred]
Inspect fossa for ooze and cystic duct stump for bile leak.

name: Choledochal Cyst Excision
source_reference: operation_id: choledochal_cyst_excision · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch71 (PDF p688–698)

name: Wilms Nephrectomy
source_reference: operation_id: wilms_nephrectomy · source: Spitz & Coran, Operative Pediatric Surgery 7E, Ch74 (PDF p722–727)
procedure_steps: Generous transverse upper-abdominal incision on the side of the tumour, extended across the contralateral rectus [EDIT: or midline xiphoid-to-below-umbilicus in older children].
Rectus sheath incised with diathermy; both rectus muscles divided; falciform ligament divided between ligatures.
Peritoneum entered — anterior tumour surface and liver protected — and the incision extended laterally under direct vision.
Abdominal contents examined for liver and peritoneal secondaries.
Contralateral kidney inspected [EDIT: anterior and posterior surfaces / at surgeon's discretion if CT done].
Lateral peritoneal attachment divided; colon and mesentery dissected off the anterior tumour surface.
Ureter and gonadal vessels ligated well below the kidney and transected.

Dissection carried caudal-to-cranial; adventitial tissue and lymph nodes swept off the great vessels [EDIT: divided between ligatures as needed]; renal vein exposed [EDIT: right side — duodenum reflected medially].
Renal vein mobilised and elevated with a vascular sling; renal artery ligated and divided first [EDIT: sequence per tumour size], then the renal vein.
Posterior aspect of the kidney mobilised by blunt dissection.
Superior dissection completed [EDIT: left — protect spleen and pancreatic tail; right — separate from liver capsule]; adrenal taken only for upper-pole tumour [EDIT: adrenal vessels ligated].
Kidney within Gerota's fascia delivered; posterior dissection completed under direct vision; renal bed inspected.
Residual para-aortic / para-caval lymph nodes excised and separately labelled for staging.
